nodes.label: Marquee Pause-on-Hover (--marquee-clicked)
nodes.rationale: .ZpRWNC:hover sets --marquee-clicked:paused so hovering the ticker stops it; :focus on the track also pauses. Motion is opt-out by intent on both pointer and keyboard.

nodes.label: Marquee Play/Pause Toggle (aria-label='Play Marquee', aria-pressed)
nodes.rationale: WCAG 2.2.2 pause/stop/hide: an auto-moving >5s marquee must offer a user-controlled pause. aria-pressed carries the play state and drives the --marquee-clicked custom property.

nodes.label: Section comp-m0ap5cxi - Text Marquee Ticker
nodes.rationale: wixui-text-marquee with --marquee-animation-state: running and --marquee-duration: 26.38s. The payload unit is cloned ~8x per track with aria-hidden duplicates purely to fill the loop, so the rebuild must emit the same clone count or the seam will show.

nodes.label: Typography Scale font_0..font_9 with --theme-spx-ratio
nodes.rationale: Sizes are fluid, not fixed: font_8 is max(14px, min(20px, calc(16 * var(--theme-spx-ratio)))). One ratio variable drives every clamp, so a rebuild must carry the same scale to match both 1440px and 390px targets.

nodes.label: MPA View Transitions (header-group / footer-group / page-group)
nodes.rationale: header/footer are hoisted to their own view-transition-name so they persist across page navigations while only the page group animates - a deliberate continuity device for a single-page-feeling site.

nodes.label: Profile Theme (#1061D3 background, data-luminance='DARK', CIRCLE_SMALL avatar)
nodes.norm_label: profile theme (#1061d3 background, data-luminance='dark', circle_small avatar)
nodes.rationale: Forced to Linktree's brand blue #1061D3 with all text #FFFFFF and DARK luminance - a default platform theme, not an OWGT palette. The linktree therefore presents a completely different colour identity from the main site, which shares no token with it.

nodes.label: Brand Palette (#1C1C1C ink, #FCED54 yellow, #FF49A6 pink, #F73D18 close red)
nodes.norm_label: brand palette (#1c1c1c ink, #fced54 yellow, #ff49a6 pink, #f73d18 close red)
nodes.rationale: Colours appear as raw hex only inside the pixel logo and the close-icon SVG; the rest of the page is driven by --color_N / --font_N custom properties. The palette is therefore split between hard-coded asset fills and tokenised theme references, which a rebuild must reconcile.

nodes.norm_label: din next w01 light (wix-hosted woff2, 3 unicode subsets)

nodes.label: Familjen Grotesk (italic 400/700, latin + latin-ext)
nodes.rationale: Bundled from the Google Fonts tag-bundler cache with display:swap and a four-weight italic/roman matrix. The italic is loaded as a separate WOFF2 from the roman, so the rebuild must ship both files or the italic hero will substitute.

nodes.label: DOM-Store Separator SVG c837a6_... (172x172, 3 brand colors)
nodes.norm_label: dom-store separator svg c837a6_... (172x172, 3 brand colors)
nodes.rationale: Inlined once into <defs id='dom-store-defs'> and re-referenced by <use href='#c837a6_...'> for every separator, so the pixel logo costs one definition regardless of marquee length. Fills are var(--svg-color-1,#1C1C1C) / #FCED54 / #FF49A6.

nodes.label: Avatar / Logo (ugc.production.linktr.ee owgt-logo.png)
nodes.rationale: Preloaded at fetchPriority=high as avatar-v3_0 and reused for the Link Sans-adjacent profile chrome, so the logo is the LCP candidate on this property.

nodes.label: Motion Enter Clip Wipe (--motion-clip-start, data-motion-enter)
nodes.rationale: Entrance reveals are clip-path polygons (e.g. polygon(0% 0%,100% 0%,100% 0%,0% 0%) plus --motion-translate-y: 100%) rather than opacity fades; the hydrated DOM shows data-motion-enter='done' meaning the reveal has already resolved.

nodes.label: Caudex Profile Typography (--profileFontFamilyThemed)
nodes.rationale: Profile heading, link text, and banner all read --profileFontFamilyThemed: Caudex with per-role weights (header 700, description 500, link 500). Again platform-default, sharing nothing with the site's Familjen Grotesk / DIN Next pairing.

nodes.label: Brand Mission Line 'Empowering Through Technology'
nodes.rationale: The single repeated OWGT tagline. It appears as the hero statement, as the marquee payload, and (as a STEM/education variant) as the Linktree bio, so it is the brand's shortest self-description across every property.

nodes.label: Footer Statement 'a 501 (c) 3 organization'
nodes.rationale: The only legal/regulatory claim anywhere on the site, and it sits in the footer rather than an About page - a deliberate low-friction placement so it never interrupts the recruitment funnel.

nodes.label: Announcement Ticker Band ('Empowering Through Technology')

nodes.label: Application Steps Block
nodes.rationale: Saturated orange-red (#e8451f-ish) full-bleed block. Dark heading 'Application Steps' at left with a pixel-art envelope icon beneath it, and two white rounded cards at right - 'Step 1 / Fill out this form.' and 'Step 2 / You will be invited for an email from oneworldgreatertogether@gmail.com...' with the two follow-on lines. nodes.label: Board Member Profile Card
nodes.rationale: White rounded card with a portrait photo, a small emoji/medal glyph before the name, the name in bold, the role in smaller text ('Vice President' for all three) and a two-to-three line bio. nodes.label: Board Cards Staggered Two-Column Layout (live @1280px)

Proof that the staggering seen in the local captures at the same width is correct behavior, not a bug - and that a responsive breakpoint sits between 1280px and 1440px.

nodes.label: Board Section (Sticky / Pinned Scroll Region)
nodes.rationale: Centered 'Board' heading followed by a tall region that behaves as a pinned/sticky scroll stage in which the three profile cards advance as the user scrolls. Because it is scroll-pinned, full-page Playwright captures render a large empty white void above the cards - this is expected capture behavior, not a layout bug, and it is why live and local screenshots both show the void.

nodes.label: Board Cards Three-Column Row (live @1440px)

nodes.label: Uncolored Inherited-Fill Silhouette Style
nodes.rationale: The arrow ships with no fill/data-color at all, so its color is decided entirely by CSS currentColor/parent. This is how one icon can serve both a light and a dark CTA without a second asset - a deliberate break from the hard-coded data-color tokens used everywhere else in the icon folder.

nodes.label: Gold Badge Palette (#F1A41D / #F4B70F / #FFEC40)
nodes.rationale: Three near-identical golds carry the reward language across the whole icon set: #F1A41D in the medal badge, #F4B70F in the ribbon badge, and #FFEC40 in every pixel sprite. Because the badge gold is shifted warmer/darker, the badges read as a slightly more premium tier than the arcade sprites.

nodes.label: Podium Step Colorway (#13336E / #E75639 / #F1A41D)
nodes.rationale: Navy #13336E and coral #E75639 are unique to this file across the entire icon folder - the arcade sprite family uses #F73D18 for its red. The podium therefore imports the site's brand navy/red rather than the sprite palette, tying the badge to the page's UI colors.

nodes.label: Accent Blue Token #4F80FF
nodes.rationale: #4F80FF appears only here, on the two ribbon tails. It is the one cool/high-chroma blue in the icon set, used to keep the ribbon from competing with the gold disc for attention.

nodes.label: Badge Medallion Disc + Rank Bars
nodes.rationale: The 29.511-radius gold circle plus three 1-unit-tall white bars (y=67.653/73.609/79.565) is the shared 'achievement roundel' primitive: a gold disc with a white emblem cut on top. Abstracting it lets badges, coins and trophies be swapped without changing the reward read.

nodes.label: Coin Arcade Tri-Color (#1C1C1C / #FFEC40 / #F73D18)
nodes.rationale: The coin is the reference instance of the arcade tri-color: near-black #1C1C1C outline/rim, #FFEC40 gold body, #F73D18 red inner ring. Every other pixel sprite in the folder reuses exactly this triple, so the coin functions as the palette anchor for the whole set.

nodes.label: Pixel Grid Raster Construction (9.427 / 10.083 Unit Module)
nodes.norm_label: pixel grid raster construction (9.427 / 10.083 unit module)
nodes.rationale: The dominant authoring convention in assets/icons: every blocky sprite snaps its rectangles to two grids - 10.083/9.427 (console, spaceinvader, icecream) and 9.428/9.427/29.594 (coin, trophies). Both are the same grid after viewBox rescaling, proving the icons were exported from a shared pixel-art source rather than drawn one by one.

nodes.label: Presentational aria-hidden Icon Wrapper
nodes.rationale: All eleven files carry role="presentation" aria-hidden="true" aria-label="" plus a duplicate data-bbox. Intent: icons are decorative only and never the sole carrier of meaning, so accessibility rests on adjacent text. Consequence: a rebuild must not add icons as the only link/button content without also providing an accessible name.

nodes.label: Wix data-color Palette Token Convention
nodes.rationale: Every non-monochrome path carries data-color="1"/"2"/"3" alongside its fill. This is a Wix Studio export artifact: it lets the live site recolor a shape group from a palette without editing the SVG. Preserved verbatim in the static rebuild so the 1:1 visual contract is not broken.

nodes.label: Arcade Console Motif
nodes.rationale: Console + space invader + coin together encode 'play/gamify'. Keeping them a named motif lets a section swap in a different set of sprites without losing the gaming signal the site's brand depends on.

nodes.label: Contact CTA Iconography
nodes.rationale: A named bucket for the small functional marks (envelope, down arrow) that sit next to buttons and links. Separating these from decorative badges prevents a rebuild from pasting arcade art into a functional affordance.

nodes.label: Soft Cream/Red Palette Divergence (#e8c96f / #ff3314)
nodes.rationale: The envelope deliberately steps outside the #1C1C1C/#FFEC40/#F73D18 sprite tri-color. Recorded because it is the strongest evidence the icon set is not palette-uniform, and any 'normalize all icons to three colors' refactor would be a visual regression.

nodes.label: Duplicate Export Pair (hero_trophy / trophy_right)
nodes.rationale: Flagged for review: the '_right' suffix implies a distinct right-facing trophy, which is exactly the kind of filename a CSS transform depends on. Any code referencing trophy_right expecting a mirrored glyph would silently get a second left-facing copy stacked on the first.

nodes.label: Retro Arcade Iconography
nodes.rationale: Umbrella concept covering the six blocky sprites (invader, console, coin, ice cream, two trophies). Defined as a concept rather than a folder node because the set spans two rendering styles: pixel-grid sprites and smooth vector badges.

nodes.label: Space Invader Motif
nodes.rationale: The single most identifiable 8-bit referent in the folder. It is the site's shorthand for 'retro game' and is therefore the motif most at risk if the icon set is restyled or subset - losing it silently degrades the brand.

nodes.label: Symmetric Sprite Lattice
nodes.rationale: The invader's left and right halves mirror on a 10.083 module, and console/coin/trophies are all built as mirrorable block runs. The shared construction rule is what makes hand-editing or recoloring these safe.

nodes.label: Arrow Down Icon (Downward Scroll Cue)
nodes.rationale: Only non-pixel icon in the set: a smooth Bézier downward arrow (single path, no fill attribute so it inherits CSS color) on a 137x160 viewBox. Sits apart from the blocky arcade sprites because it is a UI affordance, not decoration - the smooth curves let it inherit the call-to-action button color instead of the fixed arcade palette.

nodes.label: Gold Medal Badge Icon (Podium Stand)
nodes.rationale: Smooth-vector gold trophy-on-podium with a 3-tier plinth: coral #E75639 middle step, navy #13336E top step, amber #F1A41D base. Unlike the pixel sprites this uses organic circular geometry, marking it as a Wix 'color'/badge element rather than an arcade sprite.

nodes.label: Ribbon Medal Badge Icon (Blue Tails + Gold Disc)
nodes.norm_label: ribbon medal badge icon (blue tails + gold disc)
nodes.rationale: Second badge variant: two #4F80FF ribbon tails crossing behind a #F4B70F circular medallion, with three white horizontal bars standing in for a rank/ribbon emblem. Thin 68.6x110.8 viewBox makes it the vertical partner to the squarer gold-medal badge.

nodes.label: Coin Icon (Pixel Ring + Star Face)
nodes.rationale: 172x172 pixel coin built from 40+ axis-aligned 9.427/29.594-unit blocks. Structurally a 9x9 (outer) plus 7x7 (inner) pixel matrix - a magnified viewBox relative to the 10.083-unit grid of the other sprites, giving the coin a chunkier, larger-tile read at the same display size.

nodes.label: Console / Handheld Game Icon
nodes.rationale: 152x172 pixel game console with a #F73D18 diagonal D-pad/face band and #FFEC40 screen glow. The 10.083-unit module is the purest expression of the sprite grid in the folder, making it the reference art for the whole arcade family.

nodes.label: Email Envelope Icon (Contact CTA)
nodes.rationale: 200x200 pixel envelope with a red #ff3314 V-flap and a #e8c96f cream body, drawn on a 6.7/20/26.7 sub-grid. It is the only file using a softer, lower-chroma palette and the only one with real drop-shadow geometry, signalling 'friendly contact' rather than 'arcade reward'.

nodes.label: Hero Trophy Icon (Hero-Scale Sprite)
nodes.rationale: 172x172 pixel cup with side handles, #FFEC40 body and #F73D18 stem highlight. Named 'hero' because the 172px square canvas matches the other hero-scale marks (coin, console) rather than the 122-162px inline sizes - i.e. it is reserved for above-the-fold display.

nodes.label: Ice Cream Cone Icon (Reward/Treat Sprite)
nodes.rationale: 153x162 pixel cone with two scoops; the #F73D18 path is only a thin cherry/drip accent. The 10.083-unit grid plus single tri-color palette identifies it as the same sprite batch as console and spaceinvader - a lighthearted 'treat' reward rather than a competitive one.

nodes.label: Space Invader Sprite (Retro Alien)
nodes.rationale: 162x122 wide alien silhouette on a 10.083-unit grid, mirrored symmetrically about x=80.67. The aspect ratio is deliberately wider than every other sprite so it can sit as a wide divider or section ornament rather than an inline bullet.

nodes.label: Trophy Right Icon (Byte-Identical Duplicate of hero_trophy)
nodes.norm_label: trophy right icon (byte-identical duplicate of hero_trophy)
nodes.rationale: Every one of the 34 path elements is character-identical to hero_trophy.svg, including the viewBox (0.813 0.82 171.043 171.012). The filename implies a mirrored/oriented variant, but no transform or flip is applied - so the file is a redundant export, not a second artwork.

nodes.label: Trophy Icon (Inline Sprite, Flipped Accent Order)
nodes.norm_label: trophy icon (inline sprite, flipped accent order)
nodes.rationale: 134x172 narrow pixel cup whose data-color order differs from the hero trophy (red = data-color 2, gold = data-color 3). Same palette, inverted token numbering - so it is a separate export rather than a re-color of hero_trophy, and must not be deduplicated by palette alone.

nodes.label: Speculation Rules (mpa-prefetch-eager, excludes /owgt)
nodes.rationale: Prefetches every same-site path except the current /owgt page. Since the only real destinations are the same-page anchors plus the Google Form, the rule mainly warms cross-property navigation.

nodes.label: Wix Thunderbolt Fully Hydrated DOM (HOME | OWGT)
nodes.norm_label: wix thunderbolt fully hydrated dom (home | owgt)
nodes.rationale: SSR + JS-hydrated DOM of the live Wix Studio site (thunderboltVersion 1.17973.0, published version 93, site id 52e99407-716a-46a1-bcc1-5484c1e73890). Captured because the 1:1 static rebuild must reproduce rendered output, not source intent, so the hydrated class/ARIA/testid hooks are the ground truth.

nodes.label: Subscribe / Follow Button (disabled)
nodes.rationale: Rendered with the disabled attribute because the organisation profile has no follower graph to join; the only true subscription path is the separate newsletter link.

nodes.rationale: The profile is statically generated from pages/%5Bprofile%5D plus _ssgManifest.js, pinned to build 866f1d24... and versioned in window.__RUNTIME_CONFIG__. The same build hash gates the chunk list, the CSS and the manifest, so the captured DOM is a single coherent snapshot.

nodes.label: JSON-LD ProfilePage + Person (sameAs, significantLink)
nodes.rationale: Declares dateCreated 2026-02-18, dateModified 2026-09-19, and a sameAs set (Instagram, YouTube, Discord, the Wix Studio site) that is the machine-readable identity graph for the whole org. The significantLink field makes the Wix site the profile's primary destination.

nodes.label: Recommendations Carousel ('Visit X's Linktree profile page')
nodes.norm_label: recommendations carousel ('visit x's linktree profile page')
nodes.rationale: ~55 unrelated profiles (musicians, coaches, resellers) are rendered below the fold by the platform. On a nonprofit's only social hub this dilutes the org's voice and drags Core Web Vitals, and it is not something OWGT configured.

nodes.label: window.__RUNTIME_CONFIG__ (analytics, ads, Stripe, Turnstile keys)
nodes.rationale: Exposes a large platform config inline: Datadog RUM tokens, Google Ad Manager network code 23324369058, Stripe publishable key, Turnstile site key, ads country targets (ID,IN,MY,AR,CO,PH,TH,EG,MA,TR,PE,CL,BR). The country list is the clearest evidence of OWGT's actual geographic reach and it appears nowhere on the main site.

nodes.label: Social Icon Row (Website, Discord, YouTube, Instagram)
nodes.norm_label: social icon row (website, discord, youtube, instagram)
nodes.rationale: Only four of the seven-plus destinations OWGT runs get an icon-row slot, and the omissions (TikTok, X) are exactly the two that do get their own full-width link cards. The icon row is for presence, the cards are for priority.

nodes.label: Bio 'Empowering students through education in Technology and STEM.'
nodes.norm_label: bio 'empowering students through education in technology and stem.'
nodes.rationale: The social-surface variant of the main site's 'Empowering Through Technology': the site drops 'students/STEM' and the Linktree drops 'GreaterTogether', so the two properties each keep the half of the message their audience has not already inferred from context.

nodes.label: Chatbase AI Help Link 543100115 ('Questions? Ask our AI.')
nodes.norm_label: chatbase ai help link 543100115 ('questions? ask our ai.')
nodes.rationale: Rendered last, after the OGGT-owned cards, as a Linktree overlay. It is third-party AI infrastructure injected into the org's own funnel - a third trust surface alongside the Wix site and the newsletter.

nodes.label: Link Card 543099325 - X / Twitter (x.com/USOWGT)
nodes.rationale: Only platform handle that deviates from the org name - @USOWGT rather than @oneworldgreatertogether - because the full name is taken on every other network.

nodes.label: OWGT Linktree Profile (linktr.ee/owgt)
nodes.rationale: A separate OWGT-owned property, captured because the main site is otherwise a closed funnel: every outbound recruitment and social route OWGT has lives in this file, and its significantLink points back at the Wix Studio site.

nodes.label: Board Member Story (leadership roster section)
nodes.rationale: The three board_member_N.jpg files are a set, not three unrelated assets: a repeating section that pairs a portrait with a name and a short personal story. The set deliberately mixes registers (formal suit, technologist, candid campfire) so the board reads as human individuals rather than a uniform executive headshot block.

nodes.label: Real-Photography Portrait Convention
nodes.rationale: The site signals authenticity by putting un-illustrated photographs of people on the page. Every human image in this asset set is a real photograph with real lighting rather than artwork, so the organisation's credibility rests on documentary evidence instead of mascot decoration.

nodes.label: EXIF Orientation Not Applied (asset defect)
nodes.rationale: board_member_2.jpg is stored with the subject lying on its side; the file carries a camera orientation flag that the raw pixels do not honour. Any renderer that ignores EXIF will show a rotated headshot. This needs a re-orientation pass (bake the rotation into pixels or re-encode from the source) before it can sit in a portrait grid next to its two upright siblings.

nodes.label: Documentary Photography Style
nodes.rationale: Available light, shallow or moderate depth of field, honest mid-action framing, no studio backdrop and no retouching. Real rooms, real faces, visible clutter: the visual grammar of proof rather than advertising, applied consistently across the programme and event images.

nodes.label: STEM Education Program (robotics and code for students)
nodes.norm_label: stem education program (robotics and code for students)
nodes.rationale: Hands-on robotics and programming for school-age students, taught peer-to-peer by older students. This is the concrete activity that every chapter runs, and it is the substantive reason the organisation exists beneath the global-mission framing.

nodes.label: World Chapter Network
nodes.rationale: A distributed set of local student chapters, each running the same robotics-and-code curriculum with its own group of kids. The org is a network of autonomous local nodes rather than one central programme, so every chapter-facing asset has to look identical enough to read as the same movement.

nodes.label: Abstract Pastel Gradient Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: Lavender, blush and powder blue with soft mist edges and no hard geometry. Chosen to feel warm, optimistic and non-corporate, and to avoid the visual noise of a photo competing with the headline. It sits opposite the saturated documentary photography used further down the page.

nodes.label: Low-Contrast Overlay Safety
nodes.rationale: The hero background is deliberately washed out to near-white with a bright centre so that dark headline text, buttons and the black-and-blue logo can sit on top of it at full contrast. It is a text canvas, not a picture; the tint is atmosphere, the emptiness is the actual job.

nodes.label: Brand Blue Accent Palette
nodes.rationale: The only saturated brand colour in the whole asset set: a medium bright blue reserved for the O W G T letterforms, paired with near-black for the mascot and the interpunct dots. Restricting blue to the wordmark keeps it identifiable as the accent rather than a background colour.

nodes.label: Logo Asset Duplication (two copies of one wordmark)
nodes.norm_label: logo asset duplication (two copies of one wordmark)
nodes.rationale: placeholder/public/owgt-logo.png and assets/images/owgt-logo.png are the same brand mark in two files at two resolutions and two crops, with the placeholder carrying far less white margin. Because both paths are plausible for a reference to resolve to, the brand can render at two different optical sizes depending on which one is picked up. Recommended fix: one canonical logo file, one path, and let CSS handle padding.

nodes.label: OWGT Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: The combined system of mascot + wordmark + blue accent. Treats the name as a single lockup that must always travel together, so the mark is never shown without the O W G T letters and the letters are never set in another typeface or colour.

nodes.label: Robot Mascot Mark (winking robot head)
nodes.rationale: A thick black outline rounded-rect head with ear pods, a ball-tipped antenna, one round eye, one winking arc and a smile. The wink is what makes the mark friendly rather than technical, and the robot motif is a direct visual pun on the organisation's STEM/robotics subject matter.

nodes.label: Hackathon Venue Co-Branding (third-party lanyards)
nodes.rationale: The yellow lanyards in the photo read as a sponsor or host brand rather than OWGT, and the venue signage is unidentifiable. It is therefore unclear whether OWGT ran this event itself, attended one, or partnered with the host. Flagged for review: the filename asserts OWGT ownership that the pixels do not support.

nodes.label: Volunteer Hackathon
nodes.rationale: An adult-facing build sprint where volunteers and mentors collaborate on a project around a shared laptop. It is the recruitment and community signal: the way an adult supporter experiences the organisation, as opposed to the students the chapters teach.

nodes.label: Asset Scaffolding Placeholder
nodes.rationale: A placeholder/ directory holding a stand-in copy of the logo, kept so a scaffolded app can boot and render something before real assets land. Standard practice, but the hazard is that it survives past the swap and the site ends up shipping two subtly different copies of the same mark.

nodes.label: Board Member Portrait 1 (night street, formal suit)
nodes.norm_label: board member portrait 1 (night street, formal suit)
nodes.rationale: Photographic, ~3:2 landscape. Night exterior: a young person in a black suit and white shirt stands on a road beside a tree wrapped in warm string lights, head bowed, hands behind back, parked white sedan behind. Palette is near-monochrome black/navy with warm amber and gold point-lighting against a deep blue sky; high contrast, low key. A solemn, formal 'what we stand for' register rather than a casual headshot, so it reads as ethos-first portraiture for the leadership roster.

nodes.label: Board Member Portrait 2 (glasses, hazy skyline, EXIF-rotated)
nodes.norm_label: board member portrait 2 (glasses, hazy skyline, exif-rotated)
nodes.rationale: Photographic, ~4:3 landscape pixel canvas but the subject is stored rotated 90 degrees (sideways head). Clear-framed glasses, olive/grey t-shirt with small chest mark, neutral soft expression. Background is a city skyline seen through glass, heavily desaturated into pale cyan/teal haze. High-key, low-contrast, cool palette. Reads as a founder/technologist headshot, the counter-register to the formal suit in board_member_1.

nodes.label: Board Member Portrait 3 (campfire, hoodie, night forest)
nodes.norm_label: board member portrait 3 (campfire, hoodie, night forest)
nodes.rationale: Photographic, ~2:3 portrait. A young person in a dark 'HURLEY' hoodie sits centred behind a large campfire in a birch/pine forest at night. Palette splits hard: saturated orange-yellow flame mass in the lower half against near-black teal-green surroundings. Deliberately candid and outdoorsy rather than studio-lit, deliberately breaking the portrait convention to add warmth and informality to the roster.

nodes.label: Chapter Activity Photo (children building a robot in a classroom)
nodes.norm_label: chapter activity photo (children building a robot in a classroom)
nodes.rationale: Photographic, wide ~3:2 landscape. Five school-age children of varied ethnicities crowd a plywood table in a sunlit classroom: one lifts a wheeled robot chassis, one types on a laptop showing syntax-highlighted code, tablets and a parts bin on the table, wire bundles and microcontrollers scattered. Palette is warm natural daylight with primary-colour clothing accents. This is the primary proof-of-programme image for the world chapter network: it shows the actual work happening with real kids, not a stock photo of a classroom.

nodes.label: Hero Background (pastel abstract gradient field)
nodes.rationale: Non-photographic / abstract render, wide ~3:2. An extremely light, high-key field of soft blended lavender, powder blue, blush pink and warm peach with faint wispy cloud/mist forms and near-white luminous centre; no text, no figures, no hard edges. Chosen as the hero canvas so overlaid headlines, CTAs and the logo stay high-contrast and legible at 1440px and 390px.

nodes.label: OWGT Wordmark (robot mascot over O-W-G-T lockup)
nodes.norm_label: owgt wordmark (robot mascot over o-w-g-t lockup)
nodes.rationale: Square raster logo on white, roughly 1236px, drawn as a friendly mascot: a thick black rounded-rect robot head with side ear pods, a top antenna and ball tip, one solid round black eye, one arc-shaped winking eye, and a curved smile. Beneath it, 'O W G T' in heavy condensed blue capitals separated by black dots. Mark and wordmark are stacked on one axis, and the generous white border on all sides makes the file safe to drop straight into a header or hero without cropping.

nodes.label: OWGT Wordmark (placeholder copy, tightly cropped)
nodes.rationale: Square raster of the same robot-head mascot and O-W-G-T lockup at roughly 575px, but cropped tight to the artwork with almost no white margin. Visually the same brand mark as assets/images/owgt-logo.png, only smaller and uncropped for padding, which means it will render at a different optical size from the same design. It sits in a placeholder/ directory, so it looks like scaffolding left behind after the real asset was moved into assets/images/.

nodes.label: Section comp-m0awavx1 - 'Application Steps'
nodes.rationale: Only two numbered steps, and step 2 names a 1-2 week email SLA to oneworldgreatertogether@gmail.com before the meeting and acceptance gates. The email is part of the published process contract, not incidental contact info.

nodes.norm_label: arham bafna - vice president (operations / new events / expansion)

nodes.norm_label: section comp-lzf9ni60 - events 'events coming soon / to be determined'

nodes.label: Section comp-lzjn6ufe - 'How to start a chapter?'
nodes.norm_label: section comp-lzjn6ufe - 'how to start a chapter?'
nodes.rationale: Federation play: fill a short form, then read a guidelines PDF. Low-friction form first, long document second, so chapter leads self-serve without a human in the loop.

nodes.label: Volunteer Incentive (100+ hrs/yr, recognition letter, board positions)
nodes.norm_label: volunteer incentive (100+ hrs/yr, recognition letter, board positions)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly monetises participation in non-cash terms (school hours, a letter, a path to leadership), so the incentive is what substitutes for salary in a youth volunteer org.

nodes.label: Section comp-m09l6er9 - 'Want to volunteer?'
nodes.rationale: Recruitment pitch that trades on reciprocity: 'For volunteering, hours and recognition will be given.' Immediately followed by the Application Steps section, so the pitch and the process are one flow.

nodes.rationale: Three trophy variants exist (hero_trophy, trophy_right, trophy) at three scales/orientations. Treating them as one motif is the cheap way to guarantee the reward section reads consistently and to spot the accidental duplicate.

nodes.label: Volunteer Hackathon Event Photo (three volunteers at a laptop)
nodes.norm_label: volunteer hackathon event photo (three volunteers at a laptop)
nodes.rationale: Photographic, wide ~3:2 landscape. Three young adults lean in over a laptop at a hackathon table, laughing; two wear yellow event lanyards, the woman a pink one with a red badge.
